title: Lit firehose jotter — micro takeaways and followups
content:
Quick dump from reading pile + ICLR hallway/remote sessions. Very rough — meant to capture the bits I want to act on or test before they evaporate.

Top-level signal: lots of small wins for long-context come from systems + heuristics (KV compression, eviction heuristics, prefix caching) rather than a single architecture magic. Operational choices matter as much as algorithmic tweaks.

1) KV-compression via low-rank transforms (paper summary)
- Idea: learn small projection matrices per layer to compress stored KV vectors; reconstruct on-demand. Offline training of projections on representative contexts.
- Claimed: 4x memory reduction for negligible perplexity loss on long-dialog benchmarks (20k tokens).
- My notes: need to check interaction with quantization — compressed vector distribution might be more sensitive to 8-bit/4-bit noise.
- Quick experiment: apply PCA-based projection to cached KV shards in our toy serving runtime, measure reconstruction error vs. cosine similarity and downstream generation drift.
- TODO: write microbench harness that inserts projection/deprojection into our batch pipeline (see PR link in linked_artifacts).

2) Low-bit stability paper (short summary)
- Cross-layer calibration + per-channel clipping improves 4-bit activation stability for decoder-only models.
- They propose tiny per-token scale adjustments during KV read that remove systematic bias.
- Intuition: quant noise accumulates in autoregressive decode; small per-step corrections stabilize.
- Idea for Redwood: combine this with our quant profiles (Optimize suggestions) and test whether the per-token correction costs are worth unit-cost savings.
- Measurement plan: 1) offline perplexity on summarization tasks; 2) sample-level quality with our lightweight evals (BLEU/ROUGE-like + hallucination probe).

3) Long-context retrieval-anchoring talk (ICLR session notes)
- Speaker emphasized hybrid: chunked retrieval + overlap-aware reranking to avoid cold-start at segment boundaries.
- Practical tip: keep an "anchor" summary vector for each long document that helps stitch nearby windows — cheap and effective.
- Could pair with our prefix cache: store anchor vectors and preferentially route queries to hosts that have anchors primed.
- Ops consideration: anchors add metadata to routing decisions — small cost but good fallback when shard misses.

4) Tiny evals + robustness probes (methods to steal)
- Design short prompt sets that stress memory fragility: repeated-name drift, long-number consistency, multi-step fact propagation. 30 prompts per probe, fast metrics.
- Keep them deterministic and seedable so regressions show up in nightly runs.
- Action: add a "memory fragility" suite to lightweight-evals repo; tag failures with model+config.

Open questions / mental TODOs
- How does projection-based KV compression interact with our streaming and continuous-batching layers? Will projection add latency spike on first deprojection? If so, can we amortize with prefetching?
- If per-token correction for low-bit quantization works, is it simpler to apply in the runtime kernel (C++) or as a small op inserted in the computation graph? Engineering tradeoffs.
- Can anchor vectors be computed cheaply at ingest time for private customers without exposing content? (Compute-only, store encrypted metadata; legal review.)

Short-term tasks (week):
- [ ] Build a tiny harness: feed long-document -> create KV cache -> apply PCA projection -> reconstruct and sample generation; log cosine similarity and delta perplexity. Owner: Mira. Target: 2026-11-22.
- [ ] Wire per-token quant-correction stub into quant testbed (Python first), run on 2 small models. Owner: Kai. Target: 2026-11-24.
- [ ] Draft a 1-pager for Solutions Eng: "Anchor vectors for context stitching" (why it helps, cost, implementation sketch). Owner: Eliot. Target: 2026-11-20.

Links/refs I want to keep nearby:
- arXiv: Efficient KV Compression for Long-context Decoding — https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01234
- Slack thread where Ryan sketched anchor ideas (see linked_artifacts)
- Our internal PR for kv compression experiments (linked_artifacts)

Random thoughts (brain-scraps):
- Could we opportunistically quantize older KV shards more aggressively (archival quant) and keep recent shards higher-fidelity? LRU-ish fidelity tiers.
- For private deployments, offer a checkbox: "compute anchors at ingest (opt-in)" to make retrieval stitching robust but let legal control.

End of dump. Will clean into a short plan + JIRA tickets next pass.

Notes-to-self: stop hoarding ideas in head; turn 2 of these into runnable experiments this sprint or they die.
